# Shipping Request Actions

A connected clause for requesting shipment booking, cancellation, or a delivery-address change. It records requests in the executing document and emits corresponding request events. Acceptance here means a new request was recorded, not that the carrier accepted or completed it.

## Actions and inputs

Every action requires `requestId`, a nonempty text identifier shared across the shipment’s request history. `requestAddressChange` also requires `address`, nonempty text containing the proposed delivery address. Missing or invalid values fail with `SHIPPING_REQUEST_ID_REQUIRED` or `SHIPPING_ADDRESS_REQUIRED`; neither field has a usable default.

- `requestShipment` records action `book`. A new request requires `/shipment/status` to be `new`; otherwise it fails with `SHIPMENT_ALREADY_REQUESTED`. It changes status to `requested` and emits **Shipment Requested**.
- `requestCancellation` records action `cancel`. A new request requires status `requested` or `accepted`; otherwise it fails with `SHIPMENT_NO_LONGER_EDITABLE`. It preserves status and emits **Shipment Cancellation Requested**.
- `requestAddressChange` records action `address`, with the same editable-status requirement. It preserves status and `/destination`, and emits **Shipping Address Change Requested**.

Each new request is stored under its `requestId` in `/shipment/requests`, with `action`, the complete `input`, and an empty `responses` dictionary. Other shipment fields are preserved. Each emitted event contains `requestId`, the complete input as `details`, and `shipmentId` taken from `/instanceKey`.

After required-input checks, an existing `requestId` is checked before shipment-status guards. Exactly matching action and complete input return `duplicate`, without another request record or event—even if the shipment status has since changed. Reusing the identifier with different input or a different action fails with `SHIPPING_REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT`.

## Connections and execution

`bindings` associates each action name with a dictionary of named connections. This type declares no default connections, automatic triggers, property bindings, or action-input defaults. Connection `params` supplies the input passed to the shipping function; a workflow request is available as its trigger but is not automatically copied into `params`.

Connections select their source through `on`: `workflow`, `channel`, `event`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated`, or `timer`. Workflow connections require an authenticated channel binding, selected by `party` or otherwise `channel`. The request functions themselves impose no particular caller role; declaring an action does not grant a viewer permission or create an obligation.

Connection `when` defaults to true; a false condition skips execution. `parameters.conditions` may add a condition for each declared action; failure raises `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. Unknown action names in this dictionary are rejected. Connection `before` runs before the shipping action. Its `after` runs only when the action returns `acceptedNew`.

All three actions use `resultContract: outcome-v1`. Their request functions return `acceptedNew` or `duplicate`; validation failures raise errors. The contract also recognizes `rejected` and `skipped`, but these request functions do not return them. `once` defaults to false. When true, only a completed `acceptedNew` execution marks the connection `fired` and suppresses later executions; duplicates do not consume it.

Timer connections require exactly one of `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. `timestamp` is a nonnegative integer Unix time in microseconds, at most 9007199254740991. Relative timers require a timestamped source and positive integer `delayMs`, at most 9007199254740; their computed deadline must also fit the timestamp range. `policy` defaults to `first`, suppressing later arming once armed; `latest` permits replacement requests. Absolute timers prohibit `delayMs` and `policy`. Optional `cancelOn` requests cancellation of the keyed timer.

Path-based sources use non-root JSON Pointers. `embedded` and `collection` sources include embedded processing unless `embed` is false. Clause and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash, or tilde. Changing an installed connection configuration requires a new clause key.

## State and confirmation

All paths refer to the document where this clause executes, including a nested instruction’s own document. `/shipment/status` supplies the guards; this clause does not initialize it to `new`. Missing status does not satisfy those guards. A missing request dictionary is treated as empty for lookup and insertion.

Connection bookkeeping lives at `/connectionState_<clauseKey>/<actionName>.<connectionName>`, initially with `armed: false` and `fired: false`. These flags describe connection execution, not shipment acceptance or delivery; absent state does not establish either flag’s value.

Carrier responses are handled separately; this clause exposes only the three request actions. The supplied response logic requires channel `carrier` and correlation to an existing request. A valid cancellation confirmation changes status to `cancelled`; a valid address-change confirmation copies the stored requested address to `/destination`. Request emission alone establishes neither outcome, nor dispatch or delivery.
